extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and commenters on EPA and federal rulemaking concerning PFAS in drinking water (e.g., water systems, laboratories, states/tribes, manufacturers, public health professionals, and public commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of Federal Register entries and notices related to PFAS and drinking water rulemaking, monitoring, methods, and related regulatory determinations intended to inform public comments and stakeholder responses. Includes proposed/final NPDWRs, monitoring rules, method approvals, risk assessments, and cross-agency requests for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLGs and MCLs for specified PFAS
rubrics_metrics.description: For six PFAS the EPA is finalizing or proposing health-based Maximum Contaminant Level Goals (MCLGs) and enforceable Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCLs): e.g., MCLGs for PFOA and PFOS at zero; individual MCLs for PFOA and PFOS at 4.0 ng/L; individual MCLGs and MCLs for PFHxS, PFNA, and HFPO-DA at 10 ng/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values are data-driven and based on the best available science and SDWA requirements; the agency considered PFAS health effects, dose-additive concerns from co-occurring PFAS, and national/state occurrence data when setting MCLGs and MCLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Index (HI) approach for PFAS mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a Hazard Index (HI) approach to protect public health from mixtures of PFHxS, HFPO-DA (GenX), PFNA, and PFBS, including finalizing or proposing an HI of 1 (unitless) as the MCLG and MCL for any mixture containing two or more of these PFAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes known toxic effects, dose-additive health concerns, and occurrence/co-occurrence in drinking water; an HI of 1 represents a level at which no known or anticipated adverse effects are expected and allows an adequate margin of safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of feasibility when setting MCLs
rubrics_metrics.description: When promulgating enforceable MCLs EPA considers feasibility, including currently available analytical methods to measure and treatment technologies to remove chemicals from drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility considerations can limit the practical MCL even when the health-based MCLG may be lower (e.g., MCLG of zero but a feasible MCL above zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory consultation with National Drinking Water Advisory Council (NDWAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Office of Ground Water and Drinking Water must consult with the National Drinking Water Advisory Council (NDWAC) as required under the Safe Drinking Water Act on proposed revisions to the PFAS NPDWR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides meeting agendas and supplementary information to enable NDWAC consultation; this is a procedural requirement in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contaminant Candidate List (CCL) inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Contaminants included on the CCL are those currently not subject to any proposed or promulgated national primary drinking water regulations, are known or anticipated to occur in public water systems, and may require regulation under the SDWA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft CCL (e.g., CCL 6) may include chemicals, chemical groups, and microbes; EPA requests public comment on the draft and on the process used to develop it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Health Benchmarks (non-enforceable) for contaminants without standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Health Benchmarks for Pharmaceuticals (HHB-Rx) and similar benchmarks provide non-enforceable drinking water levels that describe potential adverse health effects for contaminants that have no drinking water standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These benchmarks are informational tools used to help identify chemicals of concern and guide further assessment or monitoring and are not regulatory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, mitigation, public notification, and reporting requirements for proposed NPDWRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed NPDWRs (e.g., for perchlorate) include requirements for water systems to conduct monitoring for the contaminant, take mitigation actions if levels exceed the MCL, provide information via public notification and Consumer Confidence Reports, and report results to their primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemakings often propose multiple MCL options and describe compliance and communication obligations for public water systems to protect consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of exposure studies: site selection and modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Site selection for multi-site studies on PFAS drinking water exposures should consider documented PFAS drinking water concentrations to include a wide range of exposure levels, enabling evaluation of exposure-response trends including effects at lower exposures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groundwater contaminant fate and transport models and water distribution system models may be necessary to identify contaminated areas and determine contamination periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory determination process under SDWA (every five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: SDWA requires EPA to determine whether to regulate at least five unregulated contaminants every five years using the Contaminant Candidate List as input; the regulatory determination evaluates whether to promulgate NPDWRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA publishes preliminary determinations with supporting rationale and requests public comment on the determinations and the process/analyses used (e.g., RD5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited approval of alternative analytical/test methods under SDWA
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may approve alternative testing methods for use in measuring contaminant levels in drinking water to determine compliance with NPDWRs using an expedited/streamlined authority (e.g., adding additional methods such as EPA Method 533 and Method 537.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expedited approach provides public water systems, laboratories, and primacy agencies timely access to validated measurement techniques, increasing flexibility and reducing monitoring costs while maintaining public health protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSCA PFAS data reporting scope and de minimis exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: TSCA reporting and recordkeeping for PFAS require manufacturers to report certain data (e.g., exposure, environmental and health effects) for PFAS manufactured in specified years; EPA may propose scope modifications and exemptions including a universal de minimis concentration exemption (proposed 0.1% by weight) and discussion of a 1.0% cut-off for 'hazard' uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions aim to maintain important reporting consistent with statutory requirements while exempting activities manufacturers are least likely to know or reasonably ascertain to reduce burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCMR methods, sampling design, and lab approval criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR), EPA seeks input on drinking water analytical methods for emerging contaminants, sampling design for UCMR cycles, and laboratory approval processes to support monitoring under SDWA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UCMR development follows SDWA's multi-step, risk-based approach and is intended to produce occurrence data to inform potential future regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and limitations of national recommended ambient water quality criteria (AWQC/HHC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft national recommended AWQC and Human Health Criteria (HHC) for PFAS reflect the latest science and EPA guidance; selection of which HHC to apply depends on the designated use of a water body (e.g., organism-only HHC for waters supporting fishable uses but not drinking water supply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National recommended HHC are not regulations; States and Tribes may consider them when adopting water quality standards under the Clean Water Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and Copper Rule Improvements (LCRI) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to the Lead and Copper Rule include requirements to replace lead and certain galvanized service lines, removal of the lead trigger level, reduction of the lead action level to 0.010 mg/L, strengthened tap sampling procedures, enhanced corrosion control, public education, support for small systems, and sampling in schools/child care facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures aim to reduce human health impacts from lead in drinking water and to improve implementability and public health protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-Year Review criteria for revising NPDWRs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Six-Year Review evaluates whether new information on health effects, treatment technologies, analytical methods, occurrence, exposure, implementation, or other factors provides a basis to support revision of existing NPDWRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review is periodic, and EPA uses it to identify candidate regulations for revision; absence of new appropriate candidates means no revisions at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRI addition criteria for PFAS (EPCRA/NDAA triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the NDAA and EPCRA, EPA may add PFAS to the Toxics Release Inventory if they meet listing criteria, including PFAS described by name in the law, any PFAS/class for which a method to measure levels in drinking water has been validated by the Administrator, and PFAS used to manufacture fluorinated polymers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether PFAS meet EPCRA section 313(d)(2) listing criteria and discusses what documents/activities would trigger automatic addition per the NDAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sewage sludge risk assessment focus and pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft risk assessments for PFAS in sewage sludge focus on populations living on or near impacted sites or who rely on products from impacted land; modeled risk pathways include drinking milk from pasture-raised cows, drinking water sourced from contaminated surface/groundwater, eating fish from impacted lakes, and eating beef or eggs from animals on impacted pastures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assessments are peer-reviewed, do not model risks for the general public, and are intended to inform potential regulatory actions under statutes such as the Clean Water Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Reports (CCR) content, delivery, and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to the CCR rule require improvements in readability and clarity, require States/territories/Tribes to report compliance monitoring data to EPA, incorporate electronic delivery options, provide supplemental lead information, and require systems serving 10,000 or more persons to provide CCRs to customers biannually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improved CCR rules enhance risk communication to consumers and improve EPA's oversight through required reporting of compliance monitoring data.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCRA hazardous constituent listing criteria (toxicity evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's criteria for listing substances as hazardous constituents under RCRA require scientific evidence from studies showing toxic, carcinogenic, mutagenic, or teratogenic effects on humans or other life forms; EPA reviewed toxicity and epidemiological studies and concluded nine PFAS meet these criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, these PFAS would be expressly identified for consideration in RCRA facility assessments and corrective actions at treatment, storage, and disposal facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA request for information on PFAS in seafood (processing water/source identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA seeks information to fill data gaps on PFAS occurrence in seafood and processing water, and on sources of contaminated processing water that may lead to PFAS entry into processed seafood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information submitted will inform future efforts to reduce dietary exposure, help identify likely routes of contamination, and inform mitigation strategies (e.g., finding uncontaminated source water for processing).
